name: Staley Rye Whiskey
desc: Part of the recent wave of micro-distilleries claiming a familial connection to the "pioneering spirit" of distillation, Indian Creek actually uses two-hundred year old copper pot stills from the original distillery. They produce a distillate that blurs the lines of what legally constitutes "rye whiskey" (note that the bottle specifies that it is "Distilled from a Rye Mash," whereas "Rye Whiskey" is part of the brand name), adding hops to the mash, salt and wood chips in the still, and inner-staves of hickory to their quarter-sized barrels. Some of these practices do have roots in American whiskey tradition: hop-teas were long used to clean out still due to the anti-microbial properties of the plant (ever wonder why hops ended up in beer in the first place?), and virgin oak casks have only been a requirement since 1964. The mash itself is a family recipe of 60% rye, 25% corn, and 15% malted barley. Bottled at 40% ABV.

name: Jack Daniel's Bonded Tennessee Whiskey

The packaging draws inspiration from the original 1895 Jack Daniel’s Tennessee Whiskey bottle. Offered in 700ml bottles, it made its debut in May 2022.

name: Clayton James Tennessee Whiskey
desc: Distilled and bottled at Tenn South Distillery, this craft Tennessee whiskey's mash bill uses locally grown white corn, wheat, and malted barley, then uses pot-stills rather than a column and a doubler or thumper as is common in American whiskey production. desc: A legendary and extraordinarily rare single malt. A 6-litre Lalique decanter holds the Guinness World Record for the most expensive whisky sold at auction — $628,000. Master whisky maker Bob Dalgarno spent two years sourcing whiskies dating from 1940 to 1991, including some of the last casks filled before WWII halted production and rare 1947 peated malts made during post-war coal rationing. Matured in sherry oak casks.
nose: A pleasing bouquet of a rare bookstore — oak, wood smoke, aged port, baking spices, citrus, and fruitcake.
palate: Viscous and coating. Chocolate, allspice, sherry, leather, and citrus flavors of extraordinary depth.
finish: Pipe tobacco, oak, dried fruits, and citrus — long, slow, and unforgettable.

name: Macallan 12 Double Cask
desc: Matured in a combination of American and European sherry-seasoned oak casks. Rich and smooth with classic Macallan character.
nose: Rich sherry, vanilla, caramel, and dried fruit.
palate: Smooth and rich — sherry, vanilla, caramel, and gentle spice.
finish: Long and sweet with sherry and vanilla.

name: Macallan 12 Sherry Oak
desc: Matured exclusively in hand-picked Oloroso sherry-seasoned European and American oak casks. The quintessential sherry bomb.
nose: Sherry, dried fruit, spice, and chocolate.
palate: Rich sherry character — dried fruit, chocolate, spice, and oak.
finish: Long and warming with sherry and spice.

name: Macallan 18 Double Cask
desc: Aged 18 years in American and European sherry-seasoned oak. A deeply complex and elegant expression of The Macallan.
nose: Rich sherry, oak, dried fruit, and caramel.
palate: Complex and full — sherry, dark fruit, chocolate, oak, and spice.
finish: Very long with sherry and oak.

name: Laphroaig 10 Year
desc: The iconic Islay single malt. Heavily peated with a distinctive medicinal, smoky character balanced by a surprising sweetness.
nose: Intense peat smoke, iodine, seaweed, and a hint of vanilla.
palate: Bold peat, medicinal notes, seaweed, and surprising sweetness.
finish: Very long and smoky with lingering sweetness.

name: Laphroaig Quarter Cask
desc: Finished in smaller quarter casks for accelerated wood interaction. Adds vanilla and caramel sweetness to the classic peated Laphroaig profile.
nose: Peat smoke, vanilla, caramel, and iodine.
palate: Sweeter than the 10 — peat, vanilla, caramel, and smoke.
finish: Long and smoky with vanilla.

name: Ardbeg 10 Year
desc: Consistently voted among the world's best whiskies, Ardbeg 10 is a heavily peated Islay single malt with extraordinary complexity.
nose: Intense peat, lemon, vanilla, and pepper.
palate: Complex — peat, citrus, vanilla, smoke, and pepper.
finish: Very long and peaty with vanilla.

name: Ardbeg Uigeadail
desc: Named after the loch that supplies Ardbeg's water. A non-chill filtered cask strength expression finished in sherry casks.
nose: Powerful peat, sherry, dark fruit, and chocolate.
palate: Complex — peat, sherry, dark fruit, smoke, and chocolate.
finish: Very long and warming with peat and fruit.

name: Lagavulin 16 Year
desc: One of the great Islay malts. Aged 16 years, Lagavulin is deeply peated with complex layers of dried fruit, spice, and seaweed.
nose: Intense peat, smoke, dried fruit, and seaweed.
palate: Rich and complex — peat, dried fruit, seaweed, and spice.
finish: Extraordinarily long with peat and fruit.

name: The Balvenie DoubleWood 12 Year
desc: Matured in traditional oak whisky casks then transferred to first-fill European oak sherry casks. A classic, approachable Speyside.
nose: Honey, vanilla, sherry fruit, and spice.
palate: Smooth and rich — honey, vanilla, sherry, and gentle spice.
finish: Long and sweet.

name: The Balvenie Caribbean Cask 14 Year
desc: Aged 14 years then finished in rum casks from the Caribbean, adding tropical fruit and sweet vanilla notes.
nose: Tropical fruit, vanilla, honey, and rum.
palate: Sweet and fruity — tropical fruit, vanilla, caramel, and oak.
finish: Long and sweet with rum and vanilla.

name: Glenlivet 12 Year
desc: One of the best-selling single malts in the world. Light, fruity, and approachable — a classic Speyside introduction.
nose: Light floral notes, vanilla, citrus, and fruit.
palate: Light and smooth — vanilla, citrus, fruit, and honey.
finish: Clean and medium with fruit.

name: Glenlivet 15 Year
desc: French oak edition — matured in a combination of American, European, and French Limousin oak casks for a unique richness.
nose: Vanilla, fruit, and spice.
palate: Rich and smooth — vanilla, fruit, caramel, and spice.
finish: Medium-long with spice.

name: Highland Park 12 Year
desc: Crafted on Orkney, the northernmost distillery in Scotland. A beautifully balanced single malt with heather-honeyed sweetness and a gentle peat smoke.
nose: Heather honey, vanilla, sherry fruit, and light peat.
palate: Balanced — honey, vanilla, sherry, light peat, and spice.
finish: Long and warming with honey and smoke.

name: Highland Park 18 Year
desc: Aged 18 years on Orkney, this expression adds depth and complexity to the classic Highland Park profile.
nose: Rich heather honey, sherry, oak, and gentle peat.
palate: Complex — honey, sherry, dark fruit, peat, and spice.
finish: Long and elegant.

name: Oban 14 Year
desc: From the tiny Oban distillery on Scotland's west coast. A wonderfully balanced Highland malt with maritime influences and light peat smoke.
nose: Honey, dried fruit, vanilla, and a hint of brine.
palate: Balanced and complex — honey, dried fruit, gentle peat, and brine.
finish: Long and warming with fruit and smoke.

name: Talisker 10 Year
desc: Made on the Isle of Skye, Talisker 10 is a maritime, peated single malt with bold smokiness and a distinctive peppery finish.
nose: Peat smoke, brine, pepper, and fruit.
palate: Bold — peat, pepper, brine, and sweet fruit.
finish: Long and warming with peat and pepper.

name: GlenDronach 12 Year
desc: Matured in a combination of Pedro Ximenez and Oloroso sherry casks. A quintessential sherry-influenced Highland single malt.
nose: Rich sherry, dark fruit, chocolate, and spice.
palate: Full and rich — sherry, dark fruit, chocolate, and oak.
finish: Long and warming with sherry and spice.

name: Aberlour A'bunadh
desc: A cask strength, non-chill filtered single malt matured exclusively in Oloroso sherry casks. Intensely sherried and incredibly complex.
nose: Intense sherry, dark fruit, chocolate, and spice.
palate: Rich and powerful — sherry, dark fruit, chocolate, and oak.
finish: Very long with sherry and spice.

name: Springbank 10 Year
desc: From one of Scotland's most traditional distilleries in Campbeltown. Partially peated, entirely produced on-site, and non-chill filtered.
nose: Light peat, brine, vanilla, and fruit.
palate: Complex — peat, brine, toffee, vanilla, and fruit.
finish: Long and complex with peat and fruit.

name: Bruichladdich Classic Laddie
desc: Unpeated Islay single malt — a departure from most Islay whiskies. Showcases the terroir of Scottish barley with a focus on flavor rather than smoke.
nose: Floral, fruit, vanilla, and honey.
palate: Light and elegant — floral, fruit, citrus, and vanilla.
finish: Medium and clean.

name: Monkey Shoulder
desc: A blend of three Speyside single malts — Glenfiddich, Balvenie, and Kininvie. Smooth, rich, and easy-drinking.
nose: Vanilla, caramel, fruit, and honey.
palate: Smooth and sweet — vanilla, caramel, fruit, and gentle spice.
finish: Medium and smooth.

name: Redbreast 12 Year
desc: Pot still Irish whiskey matured in a combination of bourbon and sherry casks. The benchmark for Irish pot still whiskey.
nose: Dried fruit, spice, vanilla, and sherry.
palate: Rich pot still character — dried fruit, sherry, vanilla, and spice.
finish: Long and complex.

name: Redbreast 15 Year
desc: Aged 15 years in bourbon and sherry casks, this expression adds depth and complexity to the classic Redbreast profile.
nose: Rich dried fruit, sherry, spice, and oak.
palate: Complex and full — dried fruit, sherry, spice, and leather.
finish: Very long and warming.

name: Redbreast Cask Strength
desc: The cask strength expression of Redbreast 12, bottled without dilution for maximum intensity.
nose: Intense dried fruit, sherry, and spice.
palate: Powerful pot still — dried fruit, sherry, spice, and oak.
finish: Very long with fruit and spice.

name: Green Spot
desc: A single pot still Irish whiskey from Mitchell & Son, matured in bourbon and sherry casks. Approachable and complex.
nose: Pot still spice, vanilla, fruit, and honey.
palate: Smooth pot still — spice, vanilla, fruit, and honey.
finish: Medium with spice and fruit.

name: Yellow Spot 12 Year
desc: Matured in bourbon, sherry, and Málaga wine casks. Uniquely complex with wine cask influence adding a distinctive character.
nose: Dried fruit, honey, spice, and wine cask sweetness.
palate: Complex — dried fruit, spice, honey, wine, and oak.
finish: Long and complex.

name: Writer's Tears Copper Pot
desc: A blend of single pot still and single malt Irish whiskeys. Named in honor of the literary giants who frequented Dublin pubs.
nose: Honey, vanilla, fruit, and floral notes.
palate: Light and smooth — honey, vanilla, fruit, and gentle spice.
finish: Clean and medium.

name: Powers John's Lane 12 Year
desc: A single pot still from the historic Powers distillery on John's Lane. Rich and complex with classic Irish pot still character.
nose: Pot still spice, dried fruit, and vanilla.
palate: Rich pot still — spice, dried fruit, oak, and honey.
finish: Long and spicy.

name: Bushmills 10 Year
desc: Single malt from the world's oldest licensed distillery, established 1608. Triple-distilled and matured in bourbon and sherry casks.
nose: Honey, vanilla, fruit, and almonds.
palate: Light and smooth — honey, vanilla, fruit, and gentle spice.
finish: Clean and medium.

name: Connemara Peated
desc: The rare peated Irish single malt. Combines the smooth, triple-distilled character of Irish whiskey with the smoke of peated barley.
nose: Light peat smoke, honey, vanilla, and fruit.
palate: Smooth with peat smoke, honey, vanilla, and fruit.
finish: Medium with smoke and honey.

name: Hibiki Japanese Harmony
desc: A blended Japanese whisky from Suntory, harmonizing malt and grain whiskies from Yamazaki, Hakushu, and Chita. Floral and delicate.
nose: Floral, honey, vanilla, and subtle spice.
palate: Delicate and complex — floral, honey, vanilla, and fruit.
finish: Long and smooth.

name: Yamazaki 12 Year
desc: Japan's first single malt, from Suntory's Yamazaki distillery. A benchmark for Japanese whisky with delicate fruit and gentle oak.
nose: Tropical fruit, peach, vanilla, and gentle oak.
palate: Delicate and complex — peach, pineapple, vanilla, and oak.
finish: Long and smooth.

name: Yamazaki 18 Year
desc: Aged 18 years across a range of cask types. A pinnacle of Japanese whisky craft, extraordinarily complex and refined.
nose: Dark fruit, oak, chocolate, and sandalwood.
palate: Complex and full — dark fruit, chocolate, oak, and spice.
finish: Extraordinarily long and complex.

name: Suntory Toki
desc: A lighter, approachable blend from Suntory designed for highball cocktails. Crisp, clean, and versatile.
nose: Honey, grapefruit, vanilla, and herb.
palate: Light and clean — honey, grapefruit, vanilla, and pepper.
finish: Clean and refreshing.

name: Nikka From the Barrel
desc: A blended Japanese whisky bottled at high proof without chill-filtration. Remarkably complex and intense for a blended whisky.
nose: Vanilla, caramel, spice, and dried fruit.
palate: Rich and complex — caramel, vanilla, spice, and oak.
finish: Long and warming.

name: Nikka Coffey Grain
desc: Made in Nikka's Coffey still, this grain whisky is unusually rich and complex for a grain, with tropical fruit and sweet vanilla.
nose: Tropical fruit, vanilla, caramel, and coconut.
palate: Smooth and sweet — tropical fruit, vanilla, caramel, and honey.
finish: Long and sweet.

name: Jack Daniel's Old No. 7
desc: The world's best-selling American whiskey. Filtered through 10 feet of sugar maple charcoal (the Lincoln County Process) before aging.
nose: Vanilla, caramel, banana, and charcoal.
palate: Sweet and smooth — vanilla, caramel, banana, and oak.
finish: Medium and sweet.

name: Jack Daniel's Gentleman Jack
desc: Double charcoal mellowed for extra smoothness — charcoal filtered before and after aging. Lighter and smoother than Old No. 7.
nose: Light vanilla, caramel, and honey.
palate: Very smooth — vanilla, caramel, honey, and banana.
finish: Clean and medium.

name: Canadian Shield Whisky
desc: The Easter Townships of Quebec, Canada is home to Domaine Pinnacle, a stone’s throw from Vermont. They’re famous for their award winning apple and ice cider but have recently branched out into spirits including this blended Canadian Whisky. It’s distilled and aged in small batches using 100% natural Canadian ingredients.
nose: A salvo of everything maple slams the sweet nose. Toffee sugar, toasted campfire marshmallows and coffee caramels setup a creamy texture that’s not at all syrupy. Cereal grains calm the nose’s sweetness as the younger grain characteristics are amplified on

name: Swear Jar Canadian Whisky
desc: This expression consists of a sourced whisky from a mash bill or rye, corn, and barley. It was distilled and aged for a minimum of 6 years in Canada. It is bottled at 40% ABV.

name: Forthwest Canadian Whisky
desc: Launched in spring 2023, Forthwest Whisky is a new whisky portfolio from Hood River Distillers. The first four whiskies include three flavored whiskies and one traditional Canadian blended whisky. This botting is the non-flavored expression made with made with five year-old Canadian whisky. It's bottled at 80 proof in a bottle made from 100% recycled glass. Availability begins in the Pacific Northwest with plans to expand nationally. (SRP $29.95)

name: High River Canadian Whisky
desc: Drew Mayville is well known as the master blender for Buffalo Trace’s collection of award winning whiskies. However, as the fourth and final master blender for the Seagram’s dynasty, he has a passion for blending Canadian whisky that includes this 2017 Sazerac release. The name pays tribute to the Canadian prairie rye grain farmed along mineral rich rivers that are prone to flooding.  This whisky is currently exclusive to Canada.
nose: A blast of cherry-heavy stone fruits transition to maple sugar aromas that slowly develop like a Polaroid picture where orange, butterscotch and hot peppery spice pulls into focus. Caramel sweetness commands the front
palate: palate with some pepper oak spice and pine. Herbal dill blends with orange pith on the pleasant
finish: finish. Assertive yet delicate like an athlete who can write poetry

name: Spicebox Canadian Spiced Whisky
desc: Spicebox Canadian Spiced Whisky was inspired by a certain Canadian distiller's Prohibition-era practice of shipping wooden barrels of whisky marked "spices" to the United States. The whisky starts off as a blend of whiskies aged for 3 to 6 years in bourbon barrels. Vanilla and spice flavors are then extracted and added to the whisky through cold infusion. The master blender admits to using three different types of vanilla beans but the exact beans and remaining spices are his secret.

name: Lord Calvert Canadian Whisky
desc: Named after Lord Calvert who, interestingly enough, actually was a real person--the first Lord Baltimore, to be exact. This spirit claims to be a "blend of choice matured whiskies." Distributed by Luxco, from Saint Louis, MO.

name: Signal Hill Canadian Whisky
desc: Signal Hill Canadian Whisky is Canadian whisky is blended and bottled in St. John’s Newfoundland. It is also named after the city’s historic Signal Hill where Guglielmo Marconi received the first wireless transatlantic message in 1901. The non-chill filtered blend contains 95% corn and 5% malted barley whiskies aged in a combination of ex-bourbon, new white oak and Canadian whisky barrels. Available across Canada, Europe and select States.
nose: A sparkling nose of vanilla, plump raisins, brown sugar, maple and rum characters highlight classic Canadian whisky spices like cloves and citrus peel. The mild oak on the nose transitions to sandalwood then branches to an easy drinking
palate: palate with a rum-like sweetness. Rye barrel spices burst with caramel, pepper and citrus zest. A refreshing bitterness compliments the rum notes through the dry cereal grain
finish: finish

name: Silk Tassel Canadian Whisky
desc: Aged in oak and bearing no age age statement, Silk Tassel is a whisky distilled in Canada and bottled at 40% ABV.

name: Legacy Blended Canadian Whisky
desc: Sazerac’s Legacy Blended Canadian whisky is an expansion of the growing Buffalo Trace Canadian whisky lineup. This whisky was blended by Master Blender, Drew Mayville and bottled at the Buffalo Trace Distillery in Frankfort, Kentucky.
nose: Creamy vanilla and maple-sweetened coffee underline the Legacy experience. Ripe orchard cherries and candy corn climb out of the creaminess. But on
palate: the palate, a welcome speck of spice dries off the nose’s fruity vanilla sweetness. This blended whisky is rich with corn that attacks the side of the mouth with a tingling
finish: finish. All accented and controlled by that O’Canada signature citrus pith

name: Last Mountain Canadian Whisky
desc: The Last Mountain Distillery is Saskatchewan Canada’s first micro-distillery located in the town of Lumsden. This blended whisky is a blend of 3-5 year old wheat whisky that’s been aged in used bourbon barrels. It’s currently only available in western Canada.

name: Mercer + Prince Canadian Whisky
desc: Mercer + Prince is a blended Canadian whisky brand made in partnership with music artist A$AP Rocky along with Global Brand Equities and E & J Gallo. The whisky is distilled, aged and blended in Canada and is aged a minimum of 4 years in American white oak barrels. Japanese Mizunara oak has been imparted in the whisky as a boisé, a method commonly used in cognac production. The brand is named after A$AP Rocky's favorite cross streets in NYC, Mercer and Prince. The bottle is designed with two cups built into it as well as the ability to lay it horizontally or vertically. Available in summer 2022.

name: Canadian Hunter Blended Canadian Whisky
desc: This is a blended whisky made in Canada. It is bottled at 80 proof.

name: Schenley O.F.C. Canadian Whisky
desc: Schenley O.F.C. was distilled at the Black Velvet Distillery in Lethbridge, Alberta. The OFC stands for “Original Fine Canadian” and no longer carries an age statement. This once very popular brand, a Canadian whisky staple for nearly a century, is getting difficult to find. Rumors are correct, it’s now discontinued but there are still cases to be found. Not available in the U.S.
nose: The initial alcohol bite coming from the bottle is accompanied by pleasant caramel, rye spice and vanilla. These flavor profiles maintain a status quo on
palate: the palate – grainy rye spice and alcohol soothed by caramel and bourbon vanilla
finish: The finish is sharp and oily but given time, an agreeable corn-fueled sweetness sets up the “Schenley” – a trademark palate cleansing citrus zest. This whisky is worth mixing into your favorite whisky drink before it’s history

name: Caribou Crossing Single Barrel Canadian Whisky
desc: Sazerac’s Caribou Crossing was designed to reinvent the Canadian whisky category. This 80 proof whisky — the first single-barrel Canadian whisky since the 19th century — is aged in oak barrels and was selected from over 200,000 barrels by Master Blender Drew Mayville.  This Canadian whisky is bottled twice a year (in the spring and fall) at the Buffalo Trace Distillery in Kentucky.
